message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is a member of the clade **Laurasiatheria**.  
Laurasiatheria is a major grouping of placental mammals that includes the orders Carnivora (to which lions belong) and Perissodactyla (to which zebras belong). The divergence that led to this clade occurred roughly 70–80 million years ago, so the last common ancestor of lion and zebra would have been a small, probably insect‑eating mammal that lived during the late Cretaceous/early Paleogene.
